problems.description: 22 naming violations and a 0.50 convention score: build.ts uses snake_case function names and non-PascalCase interfaces/classes, inconsistent with the PascalCase types (User, Item) of the seed file it replaced
Cognitive complexity +141 across the greenfield code, suggesting the build logic is concentrated in a few deeply nested functions rather than decomposed
+8 code smells and +2.9% duplication indicate repeated logic, likely in frontmatter parsing or HTML rendering
Analyzer flags build.test.ts for PascalCase/UPPER_CASE rules, but the visible test helpers (tmpDir, writeMarkdown) are camelCase — possibly analyzer noise, not real debt

strengths: Strong 169-line test suite covering edge cases: XSS escaping, date-descending sort, empty content dir, fallback titles, and code blocks, with proper tmp-dir lifecycle hygiene
Correctly pivoted the story codebase from the off-domain auth-API seed to the static-site-generator domain in src/ (greenfield)
commit_reviews.summary: A directionally correct greenfield foundation with strong tests and zero bugs, dragged down by naming-convention debt (0.50) and a high-complexity build function; the analyzer's complaints about the test file's naming appear to be false positives given its camelCase helpers.

problems.description: Convention score 0.50 with 22 naming violations across build.ts, index.ts, build.test.ts: snake_case functions in TypeScript, functions not camelCase, classes/interfaces not PascalCase, constants not UPPER_CASE. Note: these checks may be generic heuristics; the snake_case-in-TS finding in build.ts is the most credible violation.
+179 cognitive complexity added in +490 lines — template/layout/partial resolution logic is likely deeply nested and hard to follow; would benefit from decomposition into smaller helpers.
+1.8% duplication — large blocks of template HTML are repeated across test fixtures (default.hbs / layouts/default.hbs and header/footer partials duplicated verbatim).
+6 SonarQube smells introduced; no new bugs.

strengths: Comprehensive test coverage of the template system including edge cases: missing-template throws, built-in template fallback, layout-in-frontmatter, partials, and index page rendering.
Tests follow existing conventions — reuses the writeMarkdown/tmpDir helpers and beforeEach/afterEach cleanup pattern already established in the file.
Adds 0 new bugs per SonarQube and keeps the diff largely test-first, specifying behavior before implementation.
commit_reviews.summary: A large, well-tested template/layout/partial feature that fits the SSG architecture but ships with heavy cognitive complexity, 1.8% duplication, and a 0.50 convention score from 22 naming violations.

compounding_issues: Committed dist/ build artifacts into git from Session 3 onward (S3-S5 each add dist/**), bloating history and risking stale-compiled-output drift vs src/
node_modules and package-lock committed wholesale in Sessions 1-2, adding thousands of lines of noise to every subsequent diff
Seed codebase (Express auth API) was entirely discarded by Session 1's greenfield rewrite — the seed's structure provided zero continuity for later sessions
Existing test suite plateaued at 27 tests through Sessions 3-4 while engine complexity grew; only Session 5 added meaningful new coverage (incremental.test.ts)

Session 4's plugin refactor concentrated all orchestration logic into SsgEngine (onStart/beforeBuild/onFile/afterBuild/onEnd pipeline), which Session 5 then grew further with cache bookkeeping — single class risks becoming the bottleneck
key_decisions: Session 1 greenfield: full replacement of seed with a markdown-to-HTML CLI (gray-matter + marked), establishing the build pipeline
Session 2: introduced a Handlebars TemplateEngine with layouts/partials/caching of compiled templates, cleanly separating presentation from content
Session 3: added a chokidar-backed dev server with live reload (serve.ts), turning the CLI into a complete tool
Session 4: refactored to a config-driven plugin architecture (Plugin interface + BuildContext + MarkdownPlugin/TemplatePlugin) — the most consequential choice, enabling extensibility
Session 5: implemented content-hash incremental builds (sha256 of source + templates) with --incremental/--clean flags and a versioned cache manifest
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality improved steadily across the arc. It opened with a minimal but correct markdown build pipeline and 15 passing tests, matured through templating and a live-reload dev server (27 tests), then underwent a genuine architectural refactor into a plugin system in Session 4 — the clearest signal of structural growth — and closed with a clean content-hash incremental cache plus a 442-line test file. Every session's tests passed (tests_passed == tests_total at each step), and each commit extended rather than destabilized the previous design; the only flat spot was the static 27-test suite during the S3-S4 integration/refactor window before Session 5 re-invested in coverage. The main persistent drags were repository hygiene (committed dist/ and node_modules) rather than code quality.
story_review.summary: A highly coherent, steadily improving story that went from a minimal greenfield CLI to a plugin-architected static site generator with live reload and incremental caching, undermined only by repository-hygiene slipups (committed dist/ and node_modules) and a mid-arc test-coverage plateau.
